title: Make your LLM app a Domain Expert: How to Build an Expert System — Christopher Lovejoy, Anterior
talk_summary: A medical-doctor-turned-AI-engineer describes building a 'domain native' LLM system where domain experts review production outputs to produce three things at once: metrics, a failure-mode ontology, and suggested domain-knowledge improvements. Those failure-mode-labeled production cases become ready-made eval datasets that engineers iterate against, with a domain-expert PM prioritizing work by which failure mode drives the north-star metric.

takeaways.technique: Failure-mode ontology tied to a north-star metric
takeaways.what_they_do: They define 1-2 metrics users actually care about (e.g. false approvals) and a taxonomy of every way the AI fails (extraction, reasoning, rules interpretation, with subtypes), then plot failure-mode frequency against the north-star metric to prioritize fixes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: designing a failure mode ontology ... identifying what are all the different ways in which my AI fails
takeaways.numbers: moved from ~95% baseline to ~99% accuracy after iterating on this system

takeaways.what_they_do: Each labeled failure mode yields a dataset of ~100 real production cases; engineers iterate against that specific set and track per-failure-mode scores across pipeline versions to avoid regressions.

takeaways.technique: Domain-expert review UI that captures label + failure mode + suggested knowledge in one pass
takeaways.what_they_do: A bespoke dashboard shows the AI output, reasoning, source record and guidelines side by side; the expert marks correct/incorrect, picks a failure mode from the ontology, and optionally writes a domain-knowledge suggestion — all in one action.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they can come in they can mark whether it's correct or incorrect and if it's incorrect then this box here is for um defining the failure mode

takeaways.technique: Domain-knowledge suggestions gated by evals before going live
takeaways.what_they_do: Non-technical domain experts propose additions to the pipeline's domain knowledge; the pipeline can use them, and eval sets decide data-driven whether the suggestion ships (auto or human-in-loop).
takeaways.evidence_quote: given this domain knowledge suggestion from a domain expert, should that go live in the platform
takeaways.numbers: same-day fix loop: prod case reviewed, knowledge added, proven by evals, live

takeaways.technique: Domain-expert PM prioritizes by failure-mode impact
takeaways.what_they_do: A domain-expert PM sits between measurement and engineering: reads failure-mode-vs-metric data, picks the failure mode to fix, and hands engineers a concrete target threshold.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I want you to fix this failure mode because I really care about it and I want you to fix it up to this performance threshold

takeaways.technique: Bespoke internal tooling over off-the-shelf for the feedback loop
takeaways.what_they_do: They built their own review/eval dashboard rather than gluing third-party tools, because it must integrate with the rest of the platform and feed the iteration loop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it probably makes most sense to do this with bespoke tooling that you build yourself because ... you want to integrate it into the rest of your platform
